morgan: Heads-up — after the access-matrix refactor canary rolled on shard7 last night I'm seeing a ~0.7% variance in service entitlements vs expected. audit shows some services got extra `svc.read` grants. :eyes:
sam: Which canary cluster exactly? shard7?
morgan: canary shard7, deploy window ~02:12 UTC. noticed in our daily entitlement-drain report.
jin: Can you paste the diff or a sample query output?
morgan: here's a small snippet from the audit log:```sql
-- rows where source='backfill' and principal changed
select principal_id, granted_role, count(*) from role_bindings where source='backfill' and granted_at > '2026-03-18' group by 1,2 order by 3 desc;
```
morgan: Not huge but consistent: 1283 extra rows with principal_id='default-service' pairing to admin-lite roles.
diane: Did the refactor include any KMS/decryption changes? We rotated keys around 02:00.
morgan: yes — default role derivation now reads encrypted attrs that are KMS-decrypted. suspect fallback when decrypt errors occurred.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: migration job `rbac-migrate-2026-03-18` finished on shard7 exit=0 duration=3m12s
sam: Exit=0 but semantics could be wrong. Maybe post-backfill job ran with older schema or the migration coalesced null -> default-service. Check txn ordering and code paths.
morgan: quick ad-hoc query: `select count(*) from role_bindings where source='backfill' and granted_at > '2026-03-18'` -> 1283 extra on shard7 compared to pre-canary snapshot.
diane: Can you run the backfill in `--check-only` (dry-run) on shard7 and dump sample rows?
morgan: running dry-run now...
morgan: result sample shows many rows where `principal_id` was NULL and our migration code coalesced to `'default-service'` (about 60% of the extras).
security-oncall: Paging sec-eng — if `default-service` has broad permissions this could be a privilege escalation vector. Pause rollout to prod? :warning:
sam: Strongly +1 pause. Create rollback plan for canary backfill and block prod rollout until we confirm. Also open ticket.
morgan: created SEC-4521 and attached logs and diffs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4521
jin: Hypothesis: code used `COALESCE(principal_id, 'default-service')` during backfill without excluding system/system-generated rows. Fix: only coalesce for rows that explicitly indicate unknown principal in our old schema, e.g. `WHERE principal_id IS NULL AND is_system = false` or preserve original principal when `is_system = true`.
diane: Also check KMS decrypt error handling — if decryption fails code may have taken a fallback branch that assigned `default-service`. We should not write bindings on decryption failures. Add explicit logging + raise.
morgan: starting rollback: `UPDATE role_bindings rb SET principal_id = rb.original_principal WHERE rb.source='backfill' AND rb.granted_at BETWEEN '2026-03-18T02:10Z' AND '2026-03-18T02:20Z';`
infra-bot: job `rbac-backfill-rollback-shard7` started pid=4231
sam: After rollback, run verification queries: `select permission, count(*) from role_bindings where granted_at > ... group by 1` and compare to pre-canary snapshot.
security-oncall: Additionally rotate any service tokens that `default-service` could have used, and temporarily add an explicit deny rule for write-level perms for `default-service` until we confirm.
diane: For the code patch: add unit tests for KMS failure mode, add migration preflight that rejects rows with `principal_id IS NULL` unless a validated mapping exists, and add a canary assertion that entitlement delta < 0.1%.
morgan: filing postmortem draft to #postmortems and assigning owners. will attach timelines and SQL diffs.
sam: :thumbsup:
morgan: update: rollback finished, infra-bot reports exit=0. I'll run verification queries and post results in 10m.
infra-bot: job `rbac-backfill-rollback-shard7` exit=0 verified_rows=1283
morgan: verification looks clean, delta back to expected snapshot. Keeping canary paused until PR with fixes merges.
diane: Thanks. After PR lands let's run a forced dry-run across all shards and validate against prod snapshots before resuming.
